title: Wireless connections: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC and infrared

videos.script: Four ways of getting data across a gap with no wire, and only three of them are radio. {{four}} Wi-Fi is the one that has to reach across a house. Bluetooth is the one that has to last a week on a coin cell. NFC is the one whose entire security is that it only works at four centimetres. And infrared is light rather than radio, which is why a remote control has to be pointed. {{each}} Underneath all of them is one trade nobody gets around: range, speed and power pull against each other. Anything that goes further either goes slower or drains more. Every decision in this lesson sits somewhere on that triangle. {{trade}} The second idea is that the air is shared. A cable is yours; a channel is not. Your router and your neighbour's are shouting in the same room, and most of what people call a slow connection is that room being full. {{air}} We finish on the one question that actually improves a home network, and it is not the one about buying a faster router.
